Fish Soup

Game Strategy

Puzzle by Alexander Bogomolny (cut-the-knot.org)

Game: Take turns claiming words. First to own three words that share one letter wins.
How to play: Click a free word (yours turn blue, computer’s red). Tick “Computer moves first” and press So, go! to let it open.
Look for the math

Nine words, a shared-letter goal — yet the game is one you already know. Layout the words in a square and each winning triple is a row, column or diagonal.

The secret board

Arrange them like this:

FISH  SOUP  SWAN
GIRL  HORN  ARMY
KNIT  VOTE  CHAT

The first row shares S, the second R, the third T; columns share I, O, A; diagonals share H and N. Claiming three words with a common letter is exactly claiming three squares in a line — tic-tac-toe. The same idea appears in the Game of Fif and in The Game of Jam on this site.

How the computer plays

Positions are 9-bit masks. The applet (after Arthur van Hoff’s demo) tries squares in the order centre, corners, edges; takes a winning move; otherwise prefers a move after which you have no immediate win; and with chance 1 in 10 picks at random — “benevolent mistakes”. With perfect play tic-tac-toe is a draw, so a careful game ends in stalemate.

Play with Computer moves first unchecked, open in the centre, and answer every threat. Can you force the draw?
